Impact & Recovery
• Recall:
• Academic impact is analogous to a headwind, decreasing the rate of student
learning (deceleration) which, in turn leads to lower attainment
• Academic recovery is analogous to a tailwind, increasing the rate of student
learning (acceleration) which, in turn leads to higher attainment
• 2019 to 2021 we examined academic impact
• 2021 to 2022 we (hope) to examine academic recovery
• It is important to note that any meaningful discussion about recovery presumes an
understanding of the magnitude of impact.

Baseline SGP: What is Recovery

• Given the negative pandemic impacts, any recovery implies learning acceleration.
• However, not all acceleration can be considered recovery

Impact & Recovery
• ELA
• Decreases in percent proficient ranged from upper single digits in lower grades to lower single
digits in higher grades.
• Median (baseline) SGPs ranged from mid 30s (lower grades) to lower 40s (higher grades)
• Impacts were categorized as moderate to large
• Mathematics
• Decreases in percent proficient was in the lower teens
• Median (baseline) SGPs ranged from the mid to upper 20s.
• Impacts were categorized as large to severe
• Moderate, large, and severe impacts likely require multiple years of above average (pre-pandemic)
growth to recover to where students would have been had the pandemic not occurred.

Exemplar Schools: Impact & Recovery
• Original discussions about examining ROI were redirected to examine Return on Activities:
• Identify outlier schools in terms of impact/recovery.
• Investigate whether activities (or lack thereof) could potentially be responsible for the
school’s outlier status.
• For schools with plausible activities leading to exemplary recovery, investigate links to
relevant investment/funding.
• Step 1 is to find these outlier schools.
• We investigated schools along two dimensions:
• Academic Impact (2019 to 2021 decrease in student learning)
• Academic Recovery (2021 to 2022 increase in student learning relative to pre-
pandemic 2018-2019 learning)

Exemplar Schools: Impact & Recovery
• As can be seen, Hawaii and its schools experienced a largely positive 2021-2022
• We’ve created Excel spreadsheets with the identified schools to help to sort
through the many potential criteria to use to select exemplar schools
• As we discussed in Portsmouth, there was some concern that of low motivation
leading to poor results. To examine we filtered on students with very low to very
high and very high to very low growth.
• Filtering out these students led to non-appreciable changes to the impact-
recovery examinations of schools.
